data.title: Filter
data.tagline: Filtering is a feature that narrows the current content collection using existing properties or conditions.
data.learningOutcome: You can define a filter condition, read the active conditions, and distinguish filtering from search and sorting.
data.description: A task list can keep only items matching owner, status, and due date; a product list can narrow by price or size. Filtering excludes items that do not meet explicit conditions. It does not interpret a free-form sentence and is not the same as sorting results.

learning.assumes: You have narrowed a shopping, task, or data list by status, price, or date.
learning.outcome: You can define a filter condition, read the active conditions, and distinguish filtering from search and sorting.

distinctions.label: Search
distinctions.explanation: A Filter narrows the current set with explicit conditions. Search uses typed words to find possibly relevant content.

explanation.title: Conditions come from existing fields
explanation.text: Incomplete, this week, and assigned to me map to task status, date, and owner fields. When several conditions combine, the interface should show what currently limits the list.

explanation.title: Results should be recoverable
explanation.text: Clearing one condition or resetting all filters should return people to the full collection. An empty state should say conditions caused it, not imply the data vanished.

data.boundary: Filtering is not search or sorting. Search finds candidates from entered words, filtering excludes by existing properties, and sorting only changes the order of current results. For example, showing incomplete tasks does not automatically put the most urgent first.

lessonPractice.title: A person wants only tasks due this week and not completed. Which design is most accurate?

options.label: Use two filters—due date is this week and status is incomplete—and show both as active above the list
options.feedback: Correct. Two known fields narrow the task set, and people can see why some tasks are absent.

options.label: Have the person type the full sentence and match only title text
options.feedback: Titles may not contain “due this week” or “incomplete”; that mistakes structured conditions for keywords.

options.label: Sort by due date so other tasks naturally disappear
options.feedback: Sorting does not remove items that fail a condition; it only changes their order.

data.agentPrompt: Add This week and Incomplete filters to the task list. Show active conditions above the list and support clearing one or resetting all. Verify combined conditions, no results, and restoration of all tasks after reset.
